summary: The candidate implements and tests a substantial partial DFlash2 dynamic-verification path: selector-lattice selected-path confidence, cross-request top-k prefix allocation, SPS cost-table budget selection, compact ragged target verification, graph token buckets, and cutoff-aware acceptance. Candidate regression/compatibility tests and independent ROCm GPU adversarial checks passed. It does not implement the original proposal's DFlash2 trained confidence head or optional sequential temperature scaling calibration; its only confidence source is uncalibrated selector-lattice probability (the source calls it suitable for later STS). End-to-end DFlash2 serving, real checkpoint loading, live graph replay, lossless semantic equivalence, and throughput were not verifiable without compatible target/draft checkpoints. Therefore this is a partial implementation and cannot be accepted as a full resolution of the open original feature request.

tests.command: On base 358c163: PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-effee240e705/venv/bin/python lightweight source/import/GPU probe plus rg for DFLASH_CONFIDENCE
tests.what_was_measured: Confirmed imports resolve to /job/repo/python, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 sees one AMD Instinct MI350X, and the recorded base has neither the confidence module nor a registered DFLASH_CONFIDENCE implementation. Full worker import initialized AITer and did not complete cleanly, so it was not treated as reproduction evidence.
At exact candidate commit: 24 candidate regression tests passed, covering configuration gates, selected-path confidence, graph tiers, budgeting, cutoff/commit helpers, and compatibility behavior.
At exact candidate commit: 26 tests and 3 subtests passed for ragged geometry/backend capability and existing DFlash overlap/buffer compatibility.
At exact candidate commit: one GPU test with 22 subtests passed against independent PyTorch numerical references for the modified shared DSpark verify-window/cutoff kernels.

tests.command: Independent inline ROCm adversarial test of ScheduleVerifyLensTopk and selector_selected_path_confidence
tests.what_was_measured: On the MI350X, a mixed-quality two-request batch with three optional verify rows allocated lengths [4, 1], zero optional budget preserved the [1, 1] anchor progress floor, and selected-path probabilities matched an independently calculated predecessor-chain softmax reference.

tests.command: rg source contract audit; python -m compileall -q modified core modules; git diff --check 358c163..9a7fdb8
tests.what_was_measured: Core modules compile and the patch is whitespace-clean. The audit found no native source changes, trained confidence-head implementation, or DFlash2 STS/calibration path; only a comment that selector likelihood is suitable for later STS.

gpu_execution.evidence: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 exposed exactly one AMD Instinct MI350X under Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015. Candidate kernel parity (22 subtests) and the independent mixed-quality scheduler/reference test ran on that GPU and passed.

remaining_counterexamples: A compatible DFlash2 checkpoint containing a trained survival/confidence head cannot exercise such a head because candidate commit 9a7fdb8 contains no confidence-head module, checkpoint loading, or inference path; it always derives confidence from selector-lattice probabilities.

A deployment requiring the proposal's optional sequential temperature scaling cannot configure or execute it because candidate commit 9a7fdb8 has no DFlash2 STS parameters, calibration loader, or application path; the only STS mention says the raw signal is suitable for later STS.

The claim of lossless end-to-end speculative semantics remains unverified for a real DFlash2 target/draft pair, including sampling, grammar, continuous batching, overlap relay, and live compact graph replay, because no compatible model weights were supplied or cached.
The claimed mixed-workload throughput benefit remains unmeasured in a live DFlash2 serving workload.
remaining_limitations: No compatible DFlash2 target/draft checkpoint was supplied or locally cached. End-to-end HTTP serving, trained-head checkpoint loading, live-engine CUDA/HIP graph replay, semantic quality equivalence, and throughput were not run.
The qualified tiny Llama fixture was not used because it validates transport/engine execution only and cannot qualify the DFlash2 model architecture or speculative semantics.

The available accelerator is reported by Torch as AMD Instinct MI350X, not the candidate report's MI355X. This review validates ROCm execution only and does not validate NVIDIA CUDA architecture behavior.

No C/C++/CUDA/HIP/FlyDSL native source changed in the candidate diff, so no native rebuild was applicable. Python kernels/JIT paths resolved from the exact candidate checkout and the private prepared cache.

The base full-worker import entered AITer initialization and did not complete cleanly; base failure evidence therefore relies on the absent feature source/registration rather than a model-serving reproduction.
